description: Coal mine off-gas is the methane that desorbs from a seam as it is cut, captured and burned. EF 3.1 lists the flow and characterises it in no category: the JRC's `Resource use, fossils` rule -- "the CF is equal to 1 for all fossil resources", EUR 29600 §4.10 -- is applied to EF's `Non-renewable energy resources from ground`, whose six flows are all in megajoules, and EF files mine off-gas one bucket over among the `Non-renewable material resources from ground`, in standard cubic metres, where `Resource use, minerals and metals` prices crustal elements in kg Sb-eq and has nothing to price a methane flow from. A fossil fuel falls between two indicators. The ecoinvent Centre states 36 MJ/Sm³ for it, which is the JRC's rule times this flow's heating value, and a `publish` ruling in `lcia-factor-rulings.json` adopts it -- the same ground #155's minerals were approved on. Unlike horticultural peat (#160), where EF's filing is a decision, here it is a gap.

expectations.title: Coal mine off-gas carries a `Resource use, fossils` factor of 36 per standard cubic metre

subject.flow_name: Gas, Mine, Off-gas, Process, Coal Mining

expectations.comment: Published as `derivation: ruled` from the ecoinvent Centre's statement. The number is the JRC's own rule arithmetic: 1.0 MJ per MJ, times 36 MJ per standard cubic metre, which ecoinvent's implementation report (v3.12, Table 6) gives as this flow's lower heating value -- the same it gives natural gas.

expectations.title: Coal mine off-gas is still published in standard cubic metres

subject.name: Gas, Mine, Off-gas, Process, Coal Mining

expectations.comment: The ruling publishes a number on the flow as EF ships it rather than converting the flow to megajoules so that a 1.0 could reach it. Converting would restate a unit EF publishes and which the merge records deliberately (#141), and would say nothing the 36 does not.

expectations.title: The six energy carriers EF characterises still carry 1.0 megajoule per megajoule
expectations.comment: Adopting a number for a seventh flow does not change the six the JRC states. Natural gas stands for the family here because it is the flow whose heating value mine off-gas shares, so a change that confused the two would show up on it.

expectations.title: At least eight proposed-factor questions are answered by a ruling
expectations.comment: Six on the 25 August 2026 build, seven with the peat decline (#160), eight with this. Bounded below, as the earlier ones are, because the count is the queue's and an answer to some other question should not fail a claim about this one.
